newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-POLICE CALLED AS CROWD INSULT AUSTRALIANS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-POLICE CALLED AS CROWD INSULT AUSTRALIANS.

text.p: Police were called to Australia's match against Somerset on Saturday after the crowd shouted insults and swore at Shane Warne and other players.
Play was stopped for a couple of minutes when umpires Nigel Plews and John Steele asked for Somerset chief executive Peter Anderson to come on to the field.
They asked Anderson to summon police, even though there were 10 security staff employed by the club at the County Ground.
Two people were ejected, but no arrests were made. The incidents were blamed on football fans.
Australia's captain, Steve Waugh, had brought the matter to the umpires' attention.
"It came from three separate sections of the crowd and I thought it got too personal," Waugh said.
"We can handle heckling. We're used to that all around the world. But this was swearing and other things and I feel it's time someone made a fuss.
"I would certainly not have said what I did to the umpires if it had not have been bad.
"Shane Warne cops a lot of this, and obviously he gets fed up with it. He's a great player, but people like this can pay to come into the ground and then hurl abuse at him," Waugh added.
"Some of the things that were being shouted were ridiculous and it does nothing for the image of cricket, especially when families are watching and there are a lot of kids around."
Anderson said there were also complaints from Somerset members "so we called police to sort it out.
"There was a group of football fans who had been to the Bristol City v Everton game the previous night. They were very drunk and the police presence was needed to stop them using bad language."
Somerset finished a rain-affected second day 108 runs ahead at 147 for three in their second innings.
Wicketkeeper Rob Turner, an emergency opener because of injury to Keith Parsons, batted with skill to reach 65 not out for his second half-century of the match.
He also survived a verbal clash with Greg Blewett at short leg.
Earlier Andy Caddick had underlined his claims for an immediate Test recall by taking two more Australian wickets to finish with five for 54 as the Aussies reached 323.

Turner added 85 with skipper Simon Ecclestone for the second wicket but Parsons has a badly broken little finger of his left hand caused when he dropped Steve Waugh off Caddick. He could miss the rest of the season.
